body:
Ethan Wallace: collecting internal feedback on the PDF readability before we do a v1.1 refresh. pls drop: (1) confusing sections, (2) edits/typos, (3) charts that need better captions/labels, (4) anything that feels "hand-wavy". link to current PDF: https://drive.google.com/redwood/benchmark-report-v1.pdf

Soojin Lee: +1. goal for v1.1 is readability + clarity, not changing conclusions. if you suggest wording changes, pls paste exact replacement text.

Alicia Perez: Design/readability notes (skim + mobile PDF view):
- p3: first spread is heavy. recommend moving the “Key takeaways” bullets up ~1/3 page and increase line spacing (it reads cramped).
- p5 chart (latency/$ by model): legend colors too similar (blue/teal). hard for colorblind folks. can we switch one to purple and add pattern or outline?
- p7 heatmap: add explicit axis labels “Region” + “Model family” (right now it’s implied).
- p10: the footnotes run into the margin on exported PDF (likely InDesign export setting). looks like a clipping issue.

Wei Chen: Copy/consistency:
- We alternate between “latency/$” and “latency per dollar.” can we pick one and stick to it? suggestion: use “latency per dollar (latency/$)” on first mention, then “latency/$” after.
- p4: “$ / 1M tokens” vs “$/1M tok” in a few places. standardize.
- p6: “EU-West” used once; elsewhere “eu-west-1”. suggest we use human readable in main body (EU (Ireland)) and put the exact region code in appendix.
- There are 2 different names for the prompt set: “Production Mix v3” vs “Prompt Set v3”. pick one.

Elliot Price: Methodology clarity issues from a docs POV:
- We mention caching, but the reader has to hunt for the policy. On p12 methodology, can we add a 2–3 sentence “Caching/batching policy” callout box with explicit: prefix caching on/off, KV cache reuse conditions, continuous batching enabled, and whether we warmed caches.
- Define prefill/decode earlier. Right now first definition is p13; people will hit charts before that.
- p14: “stability gate” is referenced but not explained. add 1 sentence: “Runs were repeated when p95 latency variance exceeded X% …”

Jonas Weber: +1 on prefill/decode. also chart captions need to say what workload the metric corresponds to. e.g., the big latency/$ figure: is that for the “production mix” aggregate? make it explicit.

Rina Kobayashi: nit: p15 table shows “concurrency = 64” but in the appendix config snippet it’s 32 for the hosted baseline. i think we changed it mid-draft. pls reconcile (and make sure we don’t accidentally publish conflicting numbers).

Ethan Wallace: super helpful. re: caching box — Elliot can you propose exact text? want to keep it non-implementation-y but unambiguous.

Elliot Price: draft callout text (feel free to edit):
“Caching & batching: All runs used Redwood’s default production serving settings, including continuous batching. Prefix/KV caching was enabled only within a single run (no cross-run cache reuse). We performed warmup requests before measurement and excluded warmup traffic from all reported metrics.”

Soojin Lee: that’s good. we should add: “we did not cache customer prompts” / “no prompt logs”?? or is that too deep for PDF.

Michael Grant: careful on “default production serving settings” — that can be interpreted as “always on for every customer.” safer: “a standard Redwood serving configuration” and we should avoid implying identical settings across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Sofia Mendes: +1. also watch “enabled only within a single run” — ok, but confirm it’s true. if yes, add “no cross-customer cache reuse” language only if we can substantiate.

Jonas Weber: substantiation: we can say “no cross-run cache reuse” confidently. “no cross-customer cache reuse” is product behavior but might be too broad as a claim. suggest keep to benchmark harness scope.

Renee Sullivan: Readability from developer empathy lens:
- p2: intro talks about “production inference economics” but never defines what a dev should do with it. add 1 sentence like “Use this to pick a model+region and estimate unit cost at your expected latency SLO.”
- Add a small glossary box somewhere early: p50/p95, throughput, latency/$.
- CTA page (last): “Start a trial” button feels PLG only. can we add second CTA: “Talk to us about Dedicated/Private sizing” (Sales will love it).

Ben Carter: +1 second CTA. Also can we add tracking params note? PDF gets shared around; we should ensure links include campaign tag `utm_campaign=benchmark_report_v1_1` (or whatever Tyler wants).

Tyler Benson: yes please. send me final link list and I’ll generate the UTM set. also note: the PDF link in appendix currently goes to /blog not /benchmarks (wrong destination).

Alicia Perez: Another design nit: some captions are 8pt gray on white = low contrast. should be at least 10pt and darker for accessibility. the methodology section especially.

Wei Chen: content edit suggestion (p8 “What did we measure?”): the paragraph is long + abstract. propose bullets:
- Workload: production-mix prompt set (prefill-heavy + decode-heavy)
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, throughput, $/1M tokens, latency/$
- Regions: NA/EU/APAC listed
- Controls: warmup, variance gates, repeated runs

Ethan Wallace: love that. pls paste exact bullets w/ formatting and I’ll drop into doc.

Wei Chen: exact replacement bullets:
“Across each model/region, we measured:
• Workload: Prompt Set v3 (production mix spanning prefill-heavy and decode-heavy requests)
• Latency: end-to-end time to first token and time per output token (reported as p50 and p95)
• Throughput: sustained tokens/sec at fixed concurrency
• Cost efficiency: $ per 1M tokens and latency per dollar (latency/$)
• Stability: repeated runs and variance checks; outliers excluded per published criteria”

Rina Kobayashi: small but important: if we mention “time to first token” in PDF, make sure we didn’t only measure “request latency.” otherwise it’s a mismatch. (I think we have TTFT for streaming runs only.)

Jonas Weber: yeah, we need to be crisp. In v1 we mostly reported end-to-end request latency (non-streaming) + p95. TTFT is on the web page, not sure about PDF. If we add TTFT language, it needs to match the data.

Ethan Wallace: ok we’ll avoid TTFT wording in v1.1 unless we verify. Wei can you adjust that bullet to “end-to-end request latency” vs TTFT.

Wei Chen: updated bullet line:
“• Latency: end-to-end request latency (reported as p50 and p95)”

Soojin Lee: edits I noticed (typos / phrasing):
- p1: “consistant” -> “consistent”
- p9: “northvirginia” -> “North Virginia” (and check if that’s the official label we want)
- p11: “We outperform” -> can we change to “We observed lower latency/$” (less absolute)
- p16: “rerun treshold” -> “rerun threshold”

Michael Grant: +1 on softening “outperform.” also check for “best” / “leading” / “unmatched” language in headings. even internal drafts can slip.

Sofia Mendes: specifically: p5 caption currently says “Best-in-class latency/$ across regions.” That’s a comparative superlative. Recommend: “Competitive latency/$ across regions” OR “Lower latency/$ in our measured configurations” with caveats.

Ethan Wallace: good catch. I’ll search for “best”, “leading”, “unmatched”, “#1”.

Alicia Perez: For the “Key takeaways” section, we should reduce jargon:
- “Kernel selection” mention in takeaway #3 is too inside baseball. Suggest rephrase to “optimized serving runtime” and leave details to methodology appendix.

Jonas Weber: agree. keep runtime details in appendix, not top-level takeaways.

Tyler Benson: reminder: if we’re doing v1.1, can we add a version stamp on cover + last page? e.g., “v1.1 (July 2025)” and a short “What changed in v1.1” note (typos, clarity, no data changes). helps when ppl forward.

Soojin Lee: +1. also include “data collected on [date range]” near methodology so people don’t assume it’s live.

Elliot Price: we should also add a line: “Benchmark results can vary by prompt distribution, context length, and concurrency. See interactive page to filter.” That reduces misinterpretation.

Renee Sullivan: +1 and add a “How to replicate” mini box? even 3 steps:
1) pick model/region
2) run our provided harness config
3) compare vs your prompts
(we can link to methodology repo)

Ethan Wallace: maybe too much for v1.1 but we can add a “Replicating these results” link callout in appendix.

Ben Carter: sales asked for “replicating” link a bunch, +1 at least link it.

Soojin Lee: ok summarizing action items for v1.1:
- Standardize terms: latency/$ labeling, $/1M tokens, prompt set name (Wei)
- Add glossary + define prefill/decode earlier (Elliot + Ethan)
- Add caching/batching policy callout w/ legal-safe phrasing (Elliot draft + Michael/Sofia review)
- Fix caption/legend accessibility (Alicia)
- Reconcile concurrency mismatch (Rina + Jonas)
- Remove/soften superlatives (“best-in-class”, “outperform”) (Ethan + Legal)
- Add cover version stamp + “what changed” note + data collection range (Ethan)
- Update all PDF links with UTMs + fix wrong appendix link (Tyler + Ben)
Reply here if I missed anything.

Ethan Wallace: :thumbsup: I’ll post a redline doc once I’ve incorporated this. target: EOD tomorrow for quick review.

Michael Grant: please tag me when the redline is ready; I’ll do a quick pass for claims language.

Sofia Mendes: same. especially headers + captions.

Alicia Perez: I’ll take a first pass at updating the legend colors + caption contrast today. will drop before/after screenshots.

Jonas Weber: I’ll confirm the concurrency numbers + run config with Rina. no surprises, but we should be consistent.

Tyler Benson: send link list when you have it (even draft). I’ll prep UTMs + share a short mapping table.

Renee Sullivan: adding one more tiny nit: p2 has “latency/$ (lower is better)” but later a chart implies higher is better. if metric is “tokens per dollar” vs “latency per dollar”, we need to make sure the directionality is crystal clear in every chart. :eyes:

Ethan Wallace: omg yes. we need a consistent “higher/lower is better” label on each metric. will audit.

Jonas Weber: confirm: for “latency per dollar” lower is better. for “throughput per dollar” higher is better. make sure we’re not mixing.

Soojin Lee: great catch. let’s add small “Direction” label next to metric definitions (glossary).
